entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Genucius Augurinus was a high magistrate of the early Roman Republic, hailing from the ancient plebeian gens Genucia.

As one of the earliest known augurs, Gnaeus Genucius Augurinus played a crucial role in the development of Roman religious and political practices.

The Genucia gens was a prominent family in the early Roman Republic, and Gnaeus Genucius Augurinus's influence can be seen in the later development of Roman augury and the Roman Senate.

Gnaeus Genucius Augurinus's significance extends to the broader history of the Roman Republic, as he was a key figure in the struggle for power between the patrician and plebeian classes.
